title: Lesson 14: Managing a Small Portfolio of Clients: Scope, Expectations, and Time
description: Keeping several engagements alive at once by defending scope as a boundary, setting expectations you can actually hold, allocating time deliberately across the whole set, and reviewing the portfolio weekly.

questions.question: An out-of-scope request arrives from one client. What is the right move?
options: Absorb the request quietly so that the client stays happy and never hears about it
Refuse the request bluntly and move on to the work already committed
Offer a re-scope conversation in the client's terms, with the trade and its cost
Delay the request so that the client eventually stops asking about it
questions.explanation: Out-of-scope work is a theft from another client's budget, so it needs a decision. Present it as the client's choice with real costs attached instead of refusing or absorbing silently.

questions.question: Why hold committed utilization below full capacity?
options: To leave room for the guaranteed surprise without abandoning another client
To bill the client for hours that were budgeted but never actually worked at all
To keep the cost of context switching at the maximum possible rate each week
To avoid configuring any client's scheduled work to run unattended
questions.explanation: An urgent issue always arrives, and a portfolio with no slack collapses on the first surprise. Reserved capacity is a deliberate cost of holding several clients, not idle time to sell.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the weekly portfolio review?
options: To measure each client's profit margin against the margins of all the others
To renegotiate every client's contract at the start of each week
To force the whole set into view so a quiet client does not quietly starve
To replace the need for any written scope agreement with any of the clients
questions.explanation: The engagement in front of you always demands attention, and the client you are not looking at is the one that starves. A fixed review forces the whole portfolio into view on a cadence.
